(4) Rel stores its rows keyed by canonical bytes, in canonical order, as the DECODED canonical dict; iteration yields copies; package-internal Rel._build and Rel._items let operators construct from already-merged rows without re-validating, and the public constructor is the only place the annotations_reason rule is applied. The generalisation the reviewer draws from the D0049 finding: a guard verifies that a record is well-formed, never that it says what its author meant — the same class as RT-10 (a binding satisfied by a target that merely exists, not one that enforces anything). A bindings_count is a cheap checksum over authorial intent for exactly the failure mode D0049 exhibited (a folded YAML list, still valid, still resolving, silently short by one). Proposed for whoever drafts M2's law/schema session: add the field as optional first (so all 106 existing records stay valid without a mass edit), backfill counts opportunistically, then tighten to required once backfilled. . (2) Rule on D0105 item 7 now, while D0105's own reasoning is fresh, rather than at whatever later sitting next needs it: a law found wrong AFTER its milestone's Session B closed is superseded FORWARD — a new law file under the CURRENT milestone's own directory (never back-dated into the closed milestone's frozen set, never an in-place edit), the old file retained and marked superseded in MANIFEST.sha256's notes, and a decision record binding old and new together. This is BRIEF §8's existing within-a- milestone rule ("write the corrected law as a new file... mark the old one superseded"), stated for the case BRIEF §8 does not yet cover: a defect surfacing after the milestone that owned the law has already closed. Closed milestones stay immutable history; corrections are always forward, never backward into them. . (3) Add a ratchet metric: governance-mechanics line count (guards + drivers + fixtures) as a fraction of kernel line count. The reviewer's caution, not a finding: this sitting's own queue (a driver copying itself over a custody member as tolerated drift, a fixture renamed to dodge pytest's discovery glob, `-B` insufficient where an env var was needed across a subprocess boundary) is each individually justified and none of it is free — and D0049 is what silent failure in that layer looks like when the load stops being free. Sustained growth in this ratio is proposed as a defect signal for the ratchet to flag, not a metric to celebrate falling. Filed as a proposal, not a ruling, because unlike (1) and (2) the reviewer offered it as a suspicion to test, not a decided rule. . A fourth item — sequence M2's tree-anchoring fix on the expectation that it REMOVES mechanism (several of the accretions above simplify away at once), and reconsider it if it does not — is planning input for M2 Session A, not a decision this record can bind to anything; carried in rationale only. | accepted | — | governance-paths | manifest: `governance/schemas/decision-record.schema.json`; file: `scripts/check_decisions.py`; file: `docs/proposals/2026-08-27-m1-boundary-sitting/README.md` |
| D0107 | A | anti_join's presence test read the whole ZxWhy annotation, letting Why decide an answer it should only explain; fixed, and its survivors now cite the absence they attest to | A review of the kernel (prompted by the M1 boundary-sitting review pass, not a red-team doc under docs/redteam/) found that `anti_join` (src/tannen/kernel/ops.py) tested presence as `annotation != right.annotations.zero` — the FULL product annotation against the FULL product zero. Under `ZxWhy`, `rel.py`'s own docstring already states that a row of `(0, {{ref}})` (net Z-count zero, still witnessed) is RETAINED, not dropped, because it is not equal to `(0, frozenset())`. Such a row therefore counted as "present" and blocked a matching left row from surviving `anti_join` — meaning a row's `Why` content (whether it happened to carry a stale witness) could change which rows a query returns, not merely explain why. Provenance is supposed to be inert (BRIEF P4): it explains the answer, it never supplies one. . Two independent things were named and both are fixed together, because the second cannot be tested without the first: . (1) THE BUG. `ops.py::anti_join` now tests presence via the BAG IMAGE — `S.multiplicity(annotation) > 0` — rather than `annotation != zero`. `semiring.py`'s now-dead `is_positive()` (docstring: "what anti_join tests") was never actually called by `anti_join` — a second instance of the same disease as (2) below, one level up: a comment asserting a wiring that was not there. Removed rather than rewired, since nothing referenced it and the corrected presence test is not naturally "positivity of one value" any more. . A FIRST DRAFT OF THIS RECORD JUSTIFIED THAT RULE AS "forget `Why`, then ask Z whether this row is really there", and gated it behind a hard `BagSemiring` requirement. Review showed both halves were wrong, and the corrected reading is the substance of this record. `_BagProduct.multiplicity` is `Z.multiplicity(z) * Why.multiplicity(why)`, a PRODUCT: it is zero when EITHER factor is zero, so the rule is symmetric, not a projection. It does not "forget Why"; it asks both and multiplies. That symmetry is not an accident and not a second bug — L1.2, as amended by D0093, states it outright: both `(0, w)` and `(n, 0_Why)` are non-zero annotations with NO bag image. `to_bag` (§3.3) and `aggregate` already read presence exactly this way, and L1.9 states `Why`'s inertness over the bag image rather than over a projection. `anti_join` now agrees with all three. The alternative put forward in review — decide presence on the Z component alone, by locating the `Why` slot structurally and stripping it — was declined for a specific reason: the projection `pi1: (n, w) -> n` IS a semiring homomorphism, but the bag image is NOT (it is multiplicative, which L1.2 asserts, and not additive: `multiplicity((1, 0_Why) + (0, w))` is 1 while each summand has multiplicity 0). The two maps disagree precisely on an empty `Why`, and adopting `pi1` for `anti_join` alone would have made it the ONLY operator whose notion of "really there" disagrees with `to_bag` and `aggregate` — trading a one-sided rule for an inconsistent one. . THE `BagSemiring` GUARD WAS ALSO WRONG AND IS GONE. It narrowed `anti_join`'s domain without saying so: L1.7's frozen law enumerates the operators needing bag structure as exactly `distinct`, `aggregate` and `to_bag`, and asserts that operators needing only a `Semiring` still work over one without it. No frozen assertion exercised `anti_join` over the `NO_BAG` fixture, so nothing went red — the narrowing was simply invisible. `anti_join` now uses the bag rule where the semiring offers one and falls back to `annotation != zero` where it does not, so the domain is unchanged. The remaining, and now deliberate, narrowing is on negatives: under `Z`, `multiplicity(-1)` raises by the cone law, where `!= zero` counted the row as present. That matches `to_bag`, which refuses a negative for the same reason; M1 has no operator that can produce one (L1.9). To the question of whether anything was affected: all four shipped semirings (`Z`, `B`, `Why`, `ZxWhy`) declare bag structure, so `B` qualifies and nothing in the tree ever called `anti_join` over a non-bag annotation outside that frozen fixture. . (2) THE MISSING ANNOTATION. A survivor's claim ("this key was absent from the right relation") is not a claim about any row on the right — no row-level ref can express it — it is a claim about the right relation AS A WHOLE, at this version. `anti_join`'s survivors now gain a witness naming `right.content_address()` (already a valid ref in the pinned grammar, refs.py) alongside whatever `Why` they already carried, via a new `_why_slot`/`_add_witness` pair in ops.py that locates the `Why` component of any semiring structurally (bare `Why`, or a product with `Why` on either side) and is a no-op for a semiring with no `Why` component (plain `Z` or `B` — nothing to enrich, matching the finding's own framing that only `ZxWhy` was ever exposed to this). . ONE REFINEMENT TO (2), FOUND BY THE FROZEN SUITE, NOT BY THE NEW TEST: the witness is added only when `right` is non-empty. `tests/laws/m1/test_l1_ops.py`'s frozen `test_l1_8_anti_join_against_empty_is_the_identity` requires `anti_join(a, empty) == a` EXACTLY — an unconditional witness broke it on the first full-suite run after this change, because an empty right relation still has a content address, and adding it changed a survivor's annotation on a call the frozen law requires to be the identity. The fix reads as the right general rule anyway, not a special case bolted on to pass a test: against a genuinely empty relation there is nothing that was actually checked, so there is nothing honest to cite; the citation only makes sense once `right` has real content to have consulted. Worth stating plainly: the new homomorphism test below did NOT catch this — `forget_why` discards `Why` unconditionally, so it cannot see whether a witness was correctly withheld, only whether presence was decided correctly. The two tests check different things and neither substitutes for the other; only the frozen law caught this one, which is itself a small argument for never touching frozen laws. . A general law was added to catch the whole class, not just this one instance: tests/test_provenance_homomorphism.py states, via Hypothesis, that forgetting `Why` commutes with the operators — `forget_why(op(r1, r2)) == op(forget_why(r1), forget_why(r2))` — the property Green, Karvounarakis & Tannen give for free over positive relational algebra (map/project/filter/union/join). `distinct`, `aggregate` and `anti_join` sit outside RA+, so the law does not hold for them by construction and has to be checked: `anti_join` failed it before this fix (reproduced against the pre-fix code before touching it) and passes after; `distinct` and `aggregate` pass as implemented, now verified rather than assumed. . THE SCOPE OF THAT LAW WAS ALSO CORRECTED IN REVIEW, and this is the more useful half of the finding. The first draft generated every annotation with a non-empty `Why`, which quietly excluded `(n, 0_Why)` — the one state where the operators outside RA+ disagree with `pi1` — and defended the exclusion in a comment claiming such a row "never arises from real operator composition". That claim was true, but it was a load-bearing invariant asserted next to the code instead of checked by it: the same shape as `is_positive`'s docstring, one level up. It is now split by which map actually applies. The RA+ operators are drawn from the WHOLE product, empty `Why` included, because RG&T covers them unconditionally — and they pass. The three outside RA+ are stated over the reachable annotations, and the restriction is EARNED by two new property tests rather than by a comment: `add` and `mul` both preserve a non-empty `Why` (so the reachable set is closed), and the operators, run over witnessed inputs, never emit an unwitnessed annotation. Two further tests pin the disagreement itself as specified behaviour instead of leaving it in the gap between two generators: that the bag image is not additive and therefore not a homomorphism at all, and that `(3, 0_Why)` has no bag image, so it does not block a left row under `ZxWhy` while blocking under `Z`. . The invariant CANNOT be moved into `Rel` itself, which would have been the tidier fix: the frozen L1.5 law `test_l1_5_mixing_semirings_is_refused_by_name` constructs `Rel(("a",), [({"a": 1}, (2, Why.zero))])` directly, so refusing an unwitnessed annotation at construction would break a frozen law. It is a reachability property, not a representation constraint, and the tests now say exactly that. | accepted | — | — | pytest: `tests/test_provenance_homomorphism.py::test_forget_why_commutes_with_anti_join`; pytest: `tests/test_provenance_homomorphism.py::test_an_empty_why_has_no_bag_image_so_it_cannot_block`; file: `src/tannen/kernel/ops.py`; file: `src/tannen/kernel/semiring.py` |
| D0108 | C | CLAUDE.md's verification block still spells lint-imports without --config, so the documented command reads no contracts at all and passes vacuously | CLAUDE.md's "Verification (run before ending any implementation session)" block lists `uv run lint-imports` as one of the five checks. Run exactly as written, from the worktree root, it prints "Could not read any configuration." and reads NO contracts. The import contracts moved out of pyproject.toml into governance/importlinter.toml as the resolution half of RT-02 (conferral ruling 3, D0063) — deliberately, because pyproject.toml is the one file the builder may freely edit and a guard's configuration is part of the guard. Every real call site was updated to pass the config explicitly: the Makefile `verify` target and scripts/custodian.sh both invoke import-linter with `--config governance/importlinter.toml`. CLAUDE.md was not, and it is the file an agent is told to follow at the start of every session. . The correct line is the one the Makefile already uses: `uv run lint-imports --config governance/importlinter.toml`, or simply `make verify`. With the config passed, the contracts do pass — 51 files, 133 dependencies, 3 contracts kept, 0 broken — so this is a documentation defect, not a broken guard. Nothing was ever unprotected in CI, which runs the Makefile. . WHY IT MATTERS ANYWAY: the failure is silent in the direction that hurts. import-linter exits non-zero on "Could not read any configuration", so an agent chaining the five checks under `set -e` sees a failure it cannot explain and may route around it; an agent running them individually and eyeballing output sees no "BROKEN" line and may read that as green. Either way the documented ritual does not check the thing it claims to check. This was hit live on 2026-08-28 while verifying D0107. | accepted | — | governance-paths | manifest: `CLAUDE.md`; file: `governance/importlinter.toml` |
| D0109 | A | Two follow-ups to D0107: anti_join's refusal of negative annotations expires at M3, and why_slot belongs to the semiring rather than to the operator that first needed it | Two things review surfaced about D0107 that are true, small, and would be expensive to rediscover. Both are recorded now, while the reasoning is fresh, rather than left for the milestone that trips over them. . (1) THE NEGATIVES NARROWING HAS AN EXPIRY DATE, AND IT IS M3. D0107 changed anti_join's presence test from `annotation != zero` to the bag image, `multiplicity(annotation) > 0`. Under `Z` those differ on negatives: `!= zero` counted a row of `-1` as present, while `Z.multiplicity(-1)` raises by the cone law, exactly as `to_bag` raises. D0107 recorded the narrowing as deliberate and justified it by L1.9 — no M1 operator can produce a negative annotation, so nothing reachable hits it. That justification is sound and it is also DATED: deltas are precisely the thing that produces negative counts, and the delta executor is M3. On the day M1's `Z` annotations start carrying retractions, anti_join over a delta relation raises instead of answering. . Raising is the right behaviour today — it is honest, it matches `to_bag`, and inventing a semantics for "absent from a relation that retracts this row" without the delta executor's model would be guessing. But it is not an answer, and M3 must supply one before it runs anti_join over a delta. The expiry is now stated at the site in ops.py, not only here, so the person changing that code reads it. . (2) `why_slot` MOVED FROM ops.py TO semiring.py. D0107 introduced it as `ops._why_slot` because anti_join was the first caller. Where a `Why` component sits inside a semiring is a structural fact ABOUT THAT SEMIRING — it is derived entirely from `name`, `left` and `right` and mentions no operator — so it belongs beside `is_bag_semiring`, which is the same kind of fact. It is now public as `semiring.why_slot`. `ops._add_witness` stays in ops.py: adding a witness for an absence is an operator's judgement about what it just proved, not a property of the algebra. This also puts the helper where the D0110 proposal would need it, which is how the misplacement was noticed. | accepted | — | — | file: `src/tannen/kernel/semiring.py`; file: `src/tannen/kernel/ops.py` |
| D0110 | C | Enforce nonzero-implies-nonempty-Why in Rel construction, which dissolves the anti_join/π₁ disagreement instead of choosing a side — blocked because a frozen M1 law constructs the value it would refuse | PROPOSED, for the owner: make `Rel` refuse an annotation that claims copies of a row it has no derivation for — nonzero in the bag-count component, `Why.zero` in the `Why` component — under any semiring carrying a `Why` (located structurally by `semiring.why_slot`, D0109). `(n, 0_Why)` asserts "n copies of this row, and there is no derivation of it", which is a contradiction in a provenance semiring, not a value. It is refused at the door or it is not refused at all. . WHY THIS IS THE RIGHT SHAPE, AND NOT MERELY TIDIER. D0107 chose the bag image over the projection `pi1: (n, w) -> n` for anti_join's presence test, on the grounds that `to_bag` and `aggregate` already decide that way. Review then established something sharper: over the REACHABLE annotations — non-empty `Why`, non-negative counts — the bag image IS additive (`mult((z1+z2, w1 | w2)) == z1+z2`, and a union of non-empty supports is non-empty), so on that subset it is a homomorphism, it agrees with `pi1` everywhere, and the choice D0107 agonised over has NO OBSERVABLE CONSEQUENCE. The two maps part company only on `(n, 0_Why)`. `test_the_bag_image_is_not_a_homomorphism` needs `(1, 0_Why)` to make its point, which is to say it proves a fact about the declared semiring rather than about anything the kernel can reach. So the honest resolution is not to pick a map: it is to make the state where they differ unconstructible, at which point the question dissolves and D0107's choice stops mattering. . WHAT IT WOULD DISSOLVE, CONCRETELY. `REACHABLE` and `ANY_ANNOTATION` in tests/test_provenance_homomorphism.py collapse to one generator, and the RA+/non-RA+ split in that file stops being load-bearing. `to_bag` becomes total over retained rows — today a retained row may have no bag image, which is why L1.4's own law has to say so. Three pinned edge tests become one invariant enforced in one place. . AND WHY IT IS NOT MERELY THEORETICAL. D0107's closure argument (`test_the_reachable_annotations_are_closed`, `test_the_operators_never_manufacture_an_empty_why`) proves witnessed-in-witnessed-out. NOTHING PROVES WITNESSED-IN. `Rel(...)` is public, and `Rel.from_value` decodes whatever a stored `rel/1` value contains with no such check — `[n, []]` decodes straight to `(n, 0_Why)`. M1 ships no ingest path (the executor's only source is `Rel.from_value(store.get_value(ref))`; cli.py and store.py build no base relations), so the door is open but nothing walks through it TODAY. The capture layer does, and it is M2. Any ingest that promotes `Z` data to `ZxWhy`, or admits a source with no ref, seeds `(n, 0_Why)` legitimately — and at that moment `test_a_survivors_witness_can_give_an_unwitnessed_row_a_bag_image` stops being an oddity pinned in a test file and becomes live behaviour: anti_join manufacturing two bag copies out of a row that had no bag image at all. That test is the alarm, not the footnote. This should land BEFORE M2 builds capture on top of the current permissiveness. | accepted | — | governance-paths | pytest: `tests/test_provenance_homomorphism.py::test_a_survivors_witness_can_give_an_unwitnessed_row_a_bag_image`; manifest: `tests/laws/m1/test_l1_rel.py`; file: `src/tannen/kernel/rel.py` |
| D0111 | A | Nothing verified that the commands CLAUDE.md tells every session to run are commands that work; the manual is now compared against make verify by a test | tests/test_operating_manual.py compares the commands in CLAUDE.md's "Verification" fenced block against the recipe of the Makefile's `verify` target — the gate CI actually runs — and fails on any divergence that changes WHAT GETS CHECKED. Three properties: every check the manual documents is one the gate runs; each is configured the way the gate configures it; and both files were actually parsed (a detector that silently matched nothing would be a fresh instance of the disease it exists to catch). . It compares by CHECK IDENTITY, not by text. The two files spell the same guard very differently on purpose — the Makefile runs `.venv/bin/python -I -P scripts/x.py` because the floor may depend only on OS tools and literally-named paths (D0063 ruling 3), while the manual spells it `uv run python scripts/x.py`. Comparing raw lines would be noise. What it compares is the guard being run and the `--config` it is given, which is the dimension D0108 lives on. . D0108's divergence sits in a `KNOWN_DIVERGENCES` map with the record id as its value, so the suite is green today while the defect is owner-blocked, and a SECOND entry cannot be added quietly. When the owner fixes CLAUDE.md the test fails saying so in as many words — "this failure is the good outcome, not a regression" — and the entry is deleted in the same sitting. . The detector is watched failing, in both directions, against fixtures rather than against the live repo: a manual naming a tool without its config is caught; a manual that agrees produces nothing; a manual naming a guard the gate does not run is caught. Without those, the comparison could be vacuously true and green — which is precisely how D0108 survived. | accepted | — | — | pytest: `tests/test_operating_manual.py::test_documented_checks_are_configured_the_way_the_gate_configures_them`; pytest: `tests/test_operating_manual.py::test_the_detector_catches_a_missing_config` |
| D0112 | A | Nothing measured whether this tree is safe to publish; tests/test_no_pii.py is now a standing structural guard, written here rather than borrowed from life-agent | tests/test_no_pii.py scans every tracked file — which is exactly the set publishing would publish — for four classes of disclosure, and fails on any that is not explicitly declared: an email address whose domain is not allowlisted, an ABSOLUTE home-directory path (`/home/<user>/…`, `/Users/<user>/…`), a credential shape (six vendor prefixes plus the `BEGIN … PRIVATE KEY` armour), and a tracked file carrying a NUL byte that is not declared binary. . PRIOR ART, CITED AND NOT VENDORED. The owner pointed at life-agent's `.githooks/pii_check.py` — 676 lines, adversarially hardened over its own K3/r23/r27 rounds (its `docs/guards.md` row 13 records it being defeated and re-earned). It was RUN against this repository for the audit below, which is an instrument use and leaves no trace. It was NOT copied in: CLAUDE.md's hard rules forbid a dependency on another constellation repo in either direction and BRIEF §9 makes a cross-repo code dependency Tier C, so importing or vendoring it would have been a door, not a convenience. The relationship is the one docs/specs/m1.md §0.1 already draws for DBSP and the Lean formalisation: prior art is cited, never restated, never vendored, and explicitly NOT a §2 concept — §2 covers the constellation's definitions, and this is repo hygiene. . THREE LESSONS TAKEN FROM IT, EACH BECAUSE IT WAS EARNED THE HARD WAY THERE. (1) The bytes decide, first: NUL is checked on content before any extension rule, so a declared suffix is permission to be binary rather than an assertion that a file is one (its r27/C8). (2) An unscannable file is a refusal, never a pass (its r23/F4) — but here a refusal is a per-file FINDING rather than an abort. This is the one place this guard deliberately differs, and the reason is a defect found live while running theirs: pointed at this repo it exited 2 on `tests/poison/custodian-tag-signer/repo.bundle` and scanned NOTHING, because the refusal raises before the scan loop. Two runs were read as clean before the short-circuit was noticed. One poison fixture must never be able to suppress three hundred files' results. (3) A noisy guard gets disabled, and a disabled guard is what lets the leak through (their own comment). Their general "path under a non-placeholder root" layer produced 59 findings on this tree and exactly ONE true positive, because its allowlist is theirs; that layer is not reproduced. The precise half is: an absolute home path names a real user on a real machine. The tilde forms this repo uses everywhere (`~/git/worktrees/…`, `~/.ssh/tannen_builder`) are conventions, not disclosures, and are untouched. . WHAT THE AUDIT FOUND (their guard, --shapes-only, over 308 tracked files and all 538 blobs in 48 commits of history). No email address at all: the single flag was `sk-ssh-ed25519@openssh.com` in a superseded `allowed_signers` blob, which is OpenSSH's spelling of a key TYPE. No private key material. No Israeli ID, passport, mobile, HK phone, HKID, honorific name, account or document-ref shape. Every commit is authored `builder@tannen` — the identity is already pseudonymous. FOUR files disclose an absolute `/home/<user>/…` path, in the tree and in history. . THOSE FOUR ARE DECLARED, NOT REDACTED, AND THE TREE DELIBERATELY MATCHES THE HISTORY. Redacting four lines of prose would leave the repository looking cleaner than it is while the original blobs stay one `git log -p` away, and the history cannot be rewritten — every rewrite invalidates the signed tags and breaks the receipt chain. One of the four is a decision record, whose text is immutable by D0045 in any case. So they sit in `KNOWN_DISCLOSURES` with a reason each, a fifth fails the suite, and a companion test fails if one is ever redacted so the count cannot quietly stop being true — the same shape D0111 gave D0108's tolerance. IT SCANS ITS OWN SOURCE, AND ITS FIRST BUG WAS EXACTLY THAT. The fixtures below are the shapes the guard looks for, written as literals; while the file was still untracked `git ls-files` never showed it to the scan, so the suite was green about a file it had never read. It stayed green through a full local `make verify` (572 passed) because the file was untracked there too. scripts/rehearse_sitting.sh found it: the sitting commits with `git add -A`, so at step 9's POST-COMMIT gate the file was tracked, the guard flagged its own email, home-path and private-key fixtures, and the driver aborted with "verify red at the close". Two conclusions, both kept. The fix is to assemble the fixture values at run time (`_j`) rather than to exempt this path — a scanner with a blind spot over its own source is a hole with no review trail, which is life-agent's own K3 D-d finding about its `PII-OK` marker. And the property is now pinned by test_the_guard_scans_its_own_source, watched failing in both directions: with the file untracked, and with a literal leaked back into it. . AND ITS SECOND BUG WAS WORSE THAN ITS FIRST, because that one at least failed loudly. test_no_credential_shape_is_tracked filtered findings with `{kind for _, kind in _CREDENTIAL_RES}` — the (kind, pattern) pairs unpacked BACKWARDS, yielding a set of compiled patterns. `kind in kinds` compares a string against a Pattern, so it was never true, the hit list was always empty, and THE GUARD'S HEADLINE ASSERTION COULD NOT FAIL UNDER ANY INPUT. It was green through the whole first day while this file carried an OpenSSH private-key header verbatim as a fixture. Nothing detected it: the fixture tests exercise `scan()`, which was correct throughout, not the aggregation in the assertion. It was found by asking why the rehearsal reported TWO failures when three were due — that is, by reading a failure report for what it did not say. D0091's lesson in a new place: a test whose subject is a filter needs the filter exercised, not just the thing it filters. . The fix is structural rather than a corrected comprehension. Every kind `scan` can emit is named once (`CREDENTIAL_KINDS`, `EMAIL_KIND`, `HOME_KIND`, `UNSCANNABLE_KIND`, `ALL_KINDS`), `scan` emits those constants instead of string literals, and test_the_kind_filters_partition_everything_the_scan_emits builds a repository violating every kind at once and proves the four assertion tests' filters cover all of them, disjointly, each selecting something. A pattern added without a sample, or a filter that stops selecting, now fails there. Watched failing three ways: the original backwards comprehension, a new pattern with no sample, and a pattern with no test. . A pleasing confirmation that it works: with the filter repaired, the guard immediately flagged this record's sibling prose — the sentence in the test file DESCRIBING the bug contained the key header it was describing. Reworded, not exempted. . AND ITS THIRD BUG WROTE TO THE REPOSITORY UNDER TEST. Every fixture spelled `git -C <tmp_path> init` / `add -A`, which reads as "operate on tmp_path" and is not: `-C` sets the directory git starts from, while GIT_DIR, GIT_INDEX_FILE and GIT_WORK_TREE taken from the environment decide which repository it ends up in, and the environment wins. A git hook exports them naming the repository being committed, and pre-commit runs hooks. So on 2026-08-30, when the twelve staged files were committed and the check-decisions hook ran these very tests, the fixtures staged their nine files into the REAL index and staged all 309 real paths as deleted. The commit was refused — by the hook, reporting the guard's own tests as failing — and `git reset` restored the index with nothing lost, HEAD and the working tree untouched throughout. . Invisible from a plain shell, which is the point: the same suite had passed a full `make verify` twice that day, because GIT_DIR is unset there. The defect existed only in the environment where the guard is most load-bearing. Fixed with `_git`, one helper that strips every GIT_* from the environment so `-C` is actually authoritative, and all ten call sites routed through it. Pinned by test_the_fixtures_cannot_touch_the_repository_under_test, which builds a victim repository, exports the two variables a hook exports, runs the fixture path, and asserts the victim's index is byte-identical. . ITS FOURTH BUG WAS IN THE TEST JUST DESCRIBED, and it is this record's best evidence for D0116. That regression test PASSED with the fix removed — it could not fail. The reproduction set GIT_WORK_TREE as well as GIT_DIR, which points `add -A` back at the victim's own work tree so the fixture's file is never reached; a hook does not set GIT_WORK_TREE. It was caught only because the fix was removed and the test watched, per D0111. A guard written to close an instance of the class, itself an instance of the class, caught by the one discipline that catches the class. The corrected version fails with the signature of the real damage — index `real.txt` becoming `leak.txt`. . | accepted | — | — | pytest: `tests/test_no_pii.py::test_the_fixtures_cannot_touch_the_repository_under_test`; pytest: `tests/test_no_pii.py::test_no_credential_shape_is_tracked`; pytest: `tests/test_no_pii.py::test_an_undeclared_binary_is_a_finding_not_a_skip`; pytest: `tests/test_no_pii.py::test_the_kind_filters_partition_everything_the_scan_emits`; pytest: `tests/test_no_pii.py::test_the_guard_scans_its_own_source`; pytest: `tests/test_no_pii.py::test_the_known_disclosures_are_still_there` |

THE TRAP, WHICH IS IN NO SINGLE ARTIFACT AND SO SURVIVED TWO PASSES OF REVIEW. D0108 is queued `blocked-on-owner`. THE SECOND HALF IS WORSE THAN THE FIRST. tests/test_operating_manual.py (D0111) tolerates this one divergence by name and carries a test that FAILS DELIBERATELY the moment the manual and the gate agree — "D0108 is FIXED ... | D0114 | A | L1.9's cone half cannot fail under any input the fragment can draw — the mirror image of D0093, and the instance that makes the ratchet proposal's mutant half load-bearing | docs/proposals/2026-08-26-law-validation-ratchet.md gains a section recording a second instance of the hole it exists to close, found at the M1 boundary rather than at the freeze, and pointing in the opposite direction from the first. . THE FINDING. tests/laws/m1/test_l1_ops.py::test_l1_9_the_fragment_preserves_the_non_negative_cone asserts `Z.multiplicity(annotation) >= 0` over every row of an evaluated plan and then calls `to_bag()`, which raises on a negative. Its inputs come from tests/laws/m1/_fragment.py's `table_rows`, which draws multiplicities with `st.integers(min_value=1, ...)`, and no operator in M1's surface subtracts. There is no draw Hypothesis can make under which the assertion is false. The claim is true and load-bearing; the law does not test it. . WHY IT IS RECORDED IN THAT PROPOSAL RATHER THAN FILED ALONE. D0093 was a law that could never PASS; this is a law that cannot FAIL. The proposal's §2 has two halves — run the frozen law against a frozen model, and require it to fail against a stated mutant — and the halves catch disjoint defects. A model catches D0093 unaided. A model catches NOTHING here: a naive transcription of an operator set with no subtraction is exactly as unable to produce a negative as the implementation, so L1.9 passes against the model as vacuously as against the package. Only the mutant half discriminates. That matters because the mutant half is the one that reads as gold-plating and gets dropped first, and this is the only known instance in this repository that the model half cannot reach. . THE FROZEN LAW IS NOT TOUCHED. L1.9 is inside the m1 seal and is not wrong — it states a true property. It is under-tested, which is a different defect with a different remedy, and the remedy is the ratchet at M2 (D0094), not an edit. CLAUDE.md's supersession route (a NEW file, the old one marked superseded) is for a law found WRONG, and applying it here would spend the frozen-oracle protocol's one heavy mechanism on a law whose text is correct. . ONE CONSEQUENCE, recorded so it is not rediscovered at M3. D0107 narrowed anti_join's presence test to the bag image, which under `Z` refuses a negative by the cone law rather than counting it present, and justified the narrowing by L1.9. D0109 dated that justification to M3, when deltas start producing retractions. If L1.9 cannot fail, the justification never rested on a proved property of the operator set — it rested on the fragment's generator never drawing one. This does not weaken D0107's fix, which stands on L1.2 as amended by D0093. It strengthens D0109's expiry: M3 owes an answer, not a re-reading of a law that was never asked the question. | accepted | — | — | file: `docs/proposals/2026-08-26-law-validation-ratchet.md`; manifest: `tests/laws/m1/test_l1_ops.py` |
| D0115 | C | Publish tannen and develop in public — requested by the owner, queued as Tier-C door external-bytes; the tree is PII-clean but vendors 594 lines of four private sibling repositories | REQUESTED BY THE OWNER 2026-08-29, queued for the M1->M2 boundary sitting, non-blocking (BRIEF §9.2): publish this repository to GitHub and develop in the open. . It is queued rather than done because it is a door, not a preference. governance/tier-c.yaml names `external-bytes` — "Bytes leaving the repo boundary: publishing, PRs to any other constellation repo, network writes outside captured oracles"; governance/policy.yaml sets `external_surface.publishing: forbidden` and its `in_repo_mechanics.excludes` names "adding a git remote, or changing the visibility of an existing one" by hand. There is no remote configured at all, so D0053's private-origin allowance does not apply either. A door needs an affirmative signature and can never be carried by silence. . FOUR THINGS THE SIGNATURE WOULD HAVE TO COVER, because none of them is separable: (1) the door itself — `gh repo create`, `git remote add origin`, push, with the default branch ending up `master`; (2) governance/policy.yaml's `publishing: forbidden` becoming an explicit scope — that file is custody-set AND in `required_signatures`, so only the owner edits and re-signs it; (3) a LICENSE at the root. There is none. policy.yaml's `licence_defaults` says code MIT, docs CC-BY-SA-4.0, and its own comment says a licence default is not a publication decision. Published without one, the repository is all-rights-reserved, which makes "develop in public" a viewing gallery rather than an invitation; (4) a ruling on concepts/snapshots/**, below, which is the only one of the four with real design work behind it. . THE BLOCKER IS NOT PII. concepts/snapshots/** holds 13 files, 627 lines. Twelve of them, 594 lines, are verbatim excerpts of FOUR other repositories, every one of them private: gfrmin/pkm (204 lines), gfrmin/proplang (177), gfrmin/life-agent (107) and — the sharp one, at 58 — concepts/snapshots/provenance-ref-grammar/renavon-adr-002.md, 58 lines of renavondata/renavon-monorepo's ADR-002, carrying internal source paths, PR numbers, a corpus size, a cost estimate, an unreleased-model reference and a candid list of that stack's known defects. Publishing tannen publishes all of it. . This cannot be fixed by deletion. The snapshots exist because scripts/check_concepts.py verifies that each cited section resolves to bytes, and CLAUDE.md makes paraphrasing an owned definition a CI failure by design — the citation discipline is the point of BRIEF §2. Three candidate mechanisms, none chosen here: (a) keep the snapshots but exclude them from the published tree, and let check_concepts.py degrade to hash-pinned citation when a snapshot is absent, so a public clone verifies the PIN and an authorised clone verifies the BYTES; (b) keep verbatim snapshots only for repositories that are themselves public, hash-pin the rest; (c) publish the siblings first, so every citation resolves publicly. And one question that may not be the owner's alone to answer: renavondata/renavon-monorepo is a commercial repository, and an excerpt of it is not obviously ours to publish. . WHAT THE PII AUDIT FOUND. Run with life-agent's own structural guard (.githooks/pii_check.py, --shapes-only) over 308 tracked files and all 538 blobs in 48 commits of history, and re-run with this repo's own guard (D0112). No email address: the single flag was `sk-ssh-ed25519@openssh.com` in a superseded allowed_signers blob, which is OpenSSH's spelling of a key type. No private key material — allowed_signers carries two ed25519 PUBLIC halves, which publishing improves rather than harms, since it lets anyone verify the signed tags and receipts. No Israeli ID, passport, mobile, HK phone, HKID, honorific-name, account or document-ref shape. No credential token of any vendor shape. Every commit is authored `builder@tannen` or `t <builder@tannen>` — the identity is already pseudonymous. budget.yaml and policy.yaml envelopes are all zero. `.gitignore` has always kept evidence/, .venv/ and .reference/ (the sibling clones) out. . FOUR files disclose an absolute `/home/<user>/...` path, in the tree and in history: decisions/0048, two applied proposals from 2026-08-24, and the M0 red-team report. They are declared rather than redacted (D0112 argues why: the history cannot be rewritten without invalidating every signed tag and breaking the receipt chain, so redacting the tree would only make the repository look cleaner than it is). One letter of username, in four places, permanently. The owner should accept that knowingly, not discover it. . TWO LIMITS ON THAT AUDIT, STATED RATHER THAN BURIED. There is no private-name layer: life-agent's guard supplements shapes with a denylist of names, employers and domains loaded from a KB mount that is not present on this machine, precisely because a bare personal name has no shape a regex can find. Neither their guard nor D0112's can catch one. And the first two runs of their guard returned exit 2 having scanned NOTHING — a NUL-carrying poison fixture makes it refuse before the scan loop — which was read as clean until the short-circuit was noticed. Both facts are why publication still needs a human to read the tree, and why this record does not claim the audit settles it. . AMENDED 2026-08-30 AFTER REVIEW — THE THREE MECHANISMS ARE NOT EQUALS, AND ONE OF THE FOUR ITEMS IS NOT A QUESTION. Mechanism (a) is recommended. It is the only one of the three that keeps this door inside this repository: (b) makes the answer depend on which siblings are public, and (c) makes publishing tannen wait on decisions about four other repositories, one of them commercial and none of them this project's to schedule. (a) needs one change to one builder-owned script and nothing from anyone else. . And the ADR-002 line should not go to the owner as an open question. Fifty-eight verbatim lines of a commercial monorepo's internal ADR — PR numbers, source paths, a corpus size, a cost estimate, an unreleased-model reference and a candid defect list — is a no, and posing it as a choice invites a yes that nobody should have to give. Under (a) it is also moot: the snapshot stays in the authorised clone, the public tree carries the pin, and the citation discipline of BRIEF §2 is unbroken in both. The owner's signature is then over three items, not four, and the fourth is a design note. . ONE CONDITION ON (a), AND IT IS NOT OPTIONAL. A degraded check_concepts.py that verifies PINS when snapshots are absent is a check whose input set is empty in exactly the configuration being shipped to the public. Today the script's hash loop runs over `record["sources"]` for each of 8 records — 13 pins. If a public clone carries a truncated or empty concepts/ directory, the loop runs fewer times or not at all, every hash comparison it would have made is skipped, and the guard reports success. That is species I of D0116's own taxonomy, installed by the fix for a publication, in the configuration nobody runs locally — which is precisely the shape that produced D0112 ①. . So: the degraded mode COUNTS the pins it verified and compares that count against a pinned expectation, and the expectation may not be derived from the same files it is checking (deriving 13 from concepts/*.yaml makes a truncated concepts/ agree with itself). It comes from an artifact the degraded path does not also skip and that the custody floor already covers. And per D0116's rule the guard is watched failing before it is believed: delete a concept record from a fixture clone, run the degraded path, require red. Without that, the act of publishing installs the tenth instance of this repository's dominant defect class, in its own publication door. . ONE OPERATIONAL CONSEQUENCE WORTH EXPECTING. A public repository invites shallow clones, zip exports and `git push` without --tags, and RT-15 is exactly that shape: a working copy arriving without tags makes the custody floor fail and the receipt clock fresh forever. The guards already refuse it (required_tags, owner_key_enrolled). What changes is that the failure stops being exotic and starts arriving as issue reports. | accepted | — | public-surface, governance-paths | config: `governance/policy.yaml#external_surface.publishing`; pytest: `tests/test_no_pii.py::test_no_credential_shape_is_tracked`; file: `concepts/snapshots/provenance-ref-grammar/renavon-adr-002.md`; file: `scripts/check_concepts.py` |
| D0116 | A | Eight instances of one class — an artifact whose value is a failure, that cannot fail — proposed as BRIEF §5 entry 12, with `enforced` redefined to mean watched-failing | docs/proposals/2026-08-29-a-check-that-cannot-fail.md drafts a twelfth entry for BRIEF §5's correct-by-default catalogue, for the owner to apply: a check that cannot fail is not a check; the failure is produced AT THE LAYER THAT MAKES THE CLAIM; a check's input set is part of the check; and `strength: enforced` therefore means watched-failing rather than collects-and-passes. . THE CLASS, WHICH IS NOT A HAZARD BUT THIS REPOSITORY'S DOMINANT DEFECT. Eight instances, each found by a different accident and none by any mechanism: D0093 (a frozen law that could never pass); D0114 (L1.9 — a frozen law that cannot fail, because the fragment's generator draws `min_value=1` and no operator subtracts); D0091 (ratchet tests that borrowed their debt from the live repo and went silent at zero); RT-10 (a binding resolves by pointing at anything that exists); D0106 item 1 / D0049 (a missing newline folded a binding into a sibling's prose — still valid YAML, still resolving); D0108 (a documented command reading zero contracts; "passes vacuously" is in its own title); and the two found writing D0112's guard today — its input set excluded itself, and its headline assertion filtered with a backwards tuple unpack so it matched no kind and could not fail under any input. . SIX OF THE EIGHT ARE IN ARTIFACTS WRITTEN TO CLOSE AN EARLIER INSTANCE OF THE SAME CLASS. That is the finding. The shape is constant — absence of a signal read as presence of the property; nothing fired, therefore fine, when nothing COULD fire — and it survives being written down. D0111 states the discipline ("watched failing, in both directions, against fixtures rather than against the live repo") and was written the day before D0112 violated it. D0114 states it about laws on the same morning D0112 instantiated it about guards. Prose is not the mechanism; the poison corpus and D0092's pass-before/fail-after rewrite are, and they hold wherever they exist. . WHY §5 AND NOT A DECISION RECORD. §5's job is to make violations unwritable rather than detectable, and every entry has the form "the lazy path is the correct path". Here the lazy path — write an assertion, see green, stop — is INDISTINGUISHABLE from success, which is precisely the property §5 exists to remove. A rule kept only in a decision record is a rule the next session may not read, which is D0063's own argument for the §9.1 amendment. . THE MECHANISM IS PROPOSED, NOT APPLIED: `bindings[]` gains an optional `watched_failing` (a pytest node id or fixture path demonstrating the bound artifact failing), resolved exactly as the binding itself is; required for `enforced` once backfilled; `unwatched` joins `unenforced` and `residue` as a ratchet metric, subject to §9.1's metric-calibration rule. Optional-first is D0106 item 1's own staging for `bindings_count`. Its limit is stated in the proposal rather than left to be discovered: `watched_failing` can point at anything that resolves — RT-10 one level up — so it converts silence into a claim rather than proving the watch is real, the same bargain `unenforced_reason` strikes and the same one the repo's evidence says works. | accepted | — | — | file: `docs/proposals/2026-08-29-a-check-that-cannot-fail.md`; pytest: `tests/test_no_pii.py::test_the_kind_filters_partition_everything_the_scan_emits` |
| D0117 | C | A verdict is one bit: an evidence record cannot say whether a law examined a hundred non-degenerate cases, sixteen, or none — and that is the artifact the Governor seam is specified to consume | PROPOSED, for the owner: `governance/schemas/evidence-record.schema.json` gains a required measure of WHAT A RUN ACTUALLY EXAMINED, alongside the verdict of whether it passed. The shape is deliberately left open here — an example count, a count of non-degenerate examples, a coverage map keyed by whatever the law's own generator reports via hypothesis `event()` — because choosing it is part of what is being asked for. What is NOT open is that today there is no field of any shape in which the answer could be written. . THE RECORD AS FROZEN. Required fields are `format_version, law_id, milestone, verdict, run_at, seed, descriptors, environment`. `verdict` is `{"enum": ["pass", "fail"]}` — one bit. `additionalProperties: false`, so the count cannot even be added OPTIONALLY by a runner that wants to emit it; the schema refuses the record. `format_version` is `{"const": 0}`, so admitting one is a format bump, and the frozen conformance vectors under tests/laws/evidence-vectors/ are regenerated with it. . WHAT THAT COSTS, CONCRETELY, TODAY. `tannen laws report` prints one row per law: state, verdict, seed, run-at, descriptor. L0.3 is an example-only law over a handful of fixtures. L1.16 is a differential oracle over twenty-two plan shapes against DuckDB, a hundred examples each. Both print `ok  pass`. Nothing anywhere in the pipeline — record, report, digest, or tag — distinguishes them, and nothing could, because the distinguishing number is not collected. . AND IT IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL, WHICH IS HOW THIS WAS FOUND. Measured 2026-08-30 under the gate's own settings — conftest.py registers `derandomize=True`, so these are exact integers reproducible on every run and every machine, not estimates. L1.16 evaluates 2200 example-draws across its 22 shapes and 865 of them compare an EMPTY result to an empty result. Per shape the effective examples run from 29 of 100 (`select-text`) to 88 of 100 (`union-then-distinct`). On an empty draw `test_l1_16_the_fragment_agrees_with_duckdb` compares `[] == []`, which is true for any implementation of anything, and `test_l1_16_no_null_ever_appears_on_either_side` executes zero assertions. So two shapes' identical `pass` stand on threefold different evidence, and no artifact this repository produces carries the number that would say so. `docs/proposals/2026-08-26-law-validation-ratchet.md` has the per-shape table. D0114 is the same fact one step further along: a law whose effective evidence is exactly zero, also printing `pass`. . THAT THE NUMBER IS DETERMINISTIC IS THE ARGUMENT, NOT A MITIGATION. 1335 effective examples out of 2200 is a fact about this repository as fixed as any hash in MANIFEST.sha256. It can be computed today, it does not vary, and there is no field in which to put it. This is not a request for a sampling estimate or a coverage heuristic; it is a request for a place to write down an integer the runner already has. . WHY THIS IS ONE STRUCTURAL FACT AND NOT THREE FINDINGS. The 2026-08-30 sweep produced three separate items — L1.16's generator draws the degenerate case most of the time (F1), `tests/test_provenance_homomorphism.py` has the same weakness in the closure proof D0107 and D0110 lean on (F2), and `tests/laws/m0/test_l0_encoding.py` loads a Grade-S vector corpus with no non-emptiness guard (F3). Each is worth its own fix and D0118 takes two of them. But they are the same fact seen three times: THE PIPELINE HAS NO PLACE TO PUT THE NUMBER THAT WOULD HAVE REVEALED ANY OF THEM. Fix the three generators and the fourth instance is still invisible. That is why this is filed separately and ahead of them. . THE PART THAT MAKES IT THE OWNER'S. The evidence record's own schema description calls it "the future belief-update stream for the Governor seam" (BRIEF §7). A belief-update stream in which every message is one bit cannot support an update whose size depends on how much was examined — which is the only kind of update a Governor over evidence would want to make. Building the seam's consumer first and discovering the wire format cannot carry the quantity is the expensive ordering. M2 is the cheap moment. . AND WHAT IS ALREADY SIGNED STAYS SIGNED. `evidence/` is gitignored and regenerated, so the artifact that crosses a milestone boundary is not the record — it is an owner-signed close tag over a HEAD at which the report said `pass` for every law in the set. m0-close is that, already signed. This proposal does not and cannot reach backwards: M0's and M1's attestations say those laws passed, and they will never say more than that. The question is only whether M2's do. | accepted | — | governance-paths | manifest: `governance/schemas/evidence-record.schema.json`; file: `docs/proposals/2026-08-26-law-validation-ratchet.md`; pytest: `tests/laws/m1/test_l1_ops.py::test_l1_9_the_fragment_preserves_the_non_negative_cone` |
| D0118 | A | 865 of L1.16's 2200 example-draws compare an empty result to an empty result — the same 865 on every run; three independent causes, no single knob reaches them, and a floor assertion is the wrong instrument for a number that is already exact | RECORDED, and written into docs/proposals/2026-08-26-law-validation-ratchet.md as the rule M2's law generators are built to. Nothing in M1 changes — tests/laws/m1/_fragment.py is frozen and sealed. . THE FINDING, IN THE NUMBERS THE GATE ITSELF PRODUCES. `_fragment.py:83` draws each table with `st.lists(..., max_size=MAX_ROWS)` and no `min_size`. conftest.py registers `derandomize=True`, so `make verify` draws the SAME examples on every run and every machine: L1.16 evaluates 2200 example-draws across its 22 shapes, and 865 of them compare an empty result to an empty result. Per shape, the EFFECTIVE examples run from 29 of 100 (`select-text`) to 88 of 100 (`union`, `union-then-distinct`) — a threefold spread, reported as one identical `pass`, and recorded nowhere. On an empty draw `test_l1_16_the_fragment_agrees_with_duckdb` compares `[] == []`, which holds for any implementation of anything, and `test_l1_16_no_null_ever_appears_on_either_side` executes zero assertions. `tests/test_provenance_homomorphism.py:66` has the same shape, and it carries `test_the_operators_never_manufacture_an_empty_why` — the closure proof D0107 cites and D0110 leans on. . THREE INDEPENDENT CAUSES, MEASURED SEPARATELY, AND NO SINGLE KNOB REACHES THEM. Attributed under a randomised sweep counting only the tables a shape's own plan reads: (i) THE ROW-LIST LENGTH — every single-source shape attributes 100% of its empty draws to an empty source, and `min_size=1` alone moves the mean empty rate 35.2% -> 17.3% with nine of 22 shapes reaching exactly 0.0%; (ii) KEY OVERLAP — joins attribute 50-77% to an empty source and the rest to misses, and drawing b/c/d's keys from a's own takes every join-shaped plan to 0.0%; (iii) PREDICATE SELECTIVITY — `select-text` sits at ~65% under every variant of the other two, because its predicate is `t = 'a'` over a six-letter alphabet with at most six rows, so nothing matches with probability (5/6)^n. . TWO OF THE THREE OBVIOUS CURES WERE MEASURED AND DO NOT WORK, WHICH IS THE USEFUL PART. Narrowing the key domain — the good idea on its face, and the one this repo already uses in test_provenance_homomorphism.py's `key_range=(-2, 2)` — moves the mean from 35.2% to 34.7%. It was measured rather than assumed, and it is nearly a no-op because the fragment's keys are ALREADY narrow: `_value("k")` is `st.one_of(st.integers(-4, 4), st.sampled_from([0, INT_MIN, INT_MAX]))`. It also moves shapes in both directions — `join` 61.5% -> 54.0%, but `anti-join-then-project` 26.0% -> 38.0%. And coupling the keys, which does fix the joins outright (every join-shaped plan to 0.0%), takes `anti-join` from 13.8% to 41.0% and `anti-join-then-project` from 26.2% to 53.8%: THERE IS NO KEY POLICY SIMULTANEOUSLY RIGHT FOR A JOIN AND AN ANTI-JOIN. That is the finding that generalises past this fragment. . A FLOOR ASSERTION ON THE NON-DEGENERATE RATE IS REFUSED, AND THE FIRST ARGUMENT AGAINST IT WAS WRONG. "A floor on a random process fails intermittently" does NOT apply to the default gate: `derandomize=True` makes 865/2200 an exact, reproducible integer, and a floor would be perfectly stable under `make verify`. That objection is withdrawn. Three better ones survive. (1) It is a threshold on a quantity that is already exact and simply unrecorded — asserting a bound on a number nobody writes down is a worse instrument than writing it down, which is D0117. (2) It IS intermittent on the one run that exists to go beyond the fixed corpus: under `make laws-sweep` (`--hypothesis-seed=N`) the rate is a genuine random variable, and seven runs of 400 draws put the per-shape spread between best and worst in the low-to-high teens, reaching 20.2pp on `join-then-project`. A floor tuned on the derandomized corpus would be red on some sweeps and green on others with no code having changed. (3) It treats the symptom: it detects a badly shaped distribution instead of producing a well-shaped one, and a single bound cannot say which of the three causes moved. . THE RULE, WHICH IS WHAT THE THREE MEASUREMENTS ARGUE FOR. Draw the degenerate case as a NAMED case rather than as a side effect of the size distribution — `st.one_of(st.just([]), st.lists(..., min_size=1, max_size=MAX_ROWS))` — and let each shape declare the case it exists to exercise: a join wants overlapping keys, an anti-join wants PARTIAL overlap, a filter wants a literal drawn from the column it filters. Then each generator reports its own shape through hypothesis `event()`, so a run reports a distribution somebody deliberately shaped instead of one somebody is policing. No threshold anywhere. | accepted | — | — | file: `docs/proposals/2026-08-26-law-validation-ratchet.md`; file: `docs/proposals/2026-08-29-a-check-that-cannot-fail.md`; manifest: `tests/laws/m1/_fragment.py` |

Whichever bound comes first wins, and for five of the eight queued records `head -40` won. Shown-of-total, measured by running the driver's own command: D0061 19/63, D0095 19/74, D0108 31/65 — whole. D0105 40/139, D0106 40/119, D0110 40/101, D0115 40/179, D0117 40/137 — cut, with nothing printed to say so. The `sed` range also stops AT the `rationale:` key line, so no record's rationale, reversibility, status, bindings or links were ever on screen, for any of the eight. . THE WORST CASE IS THE ONE-WAY DOOR. This was not reasoned about; it was observed in a full m1 rehearsal transcript. The last line the owner sees for D0115 — the Tier-C `external-bytes` publication door — is "Publishing tannen publishes all of it." The next thing on screen is the signing prompt. Never shown: the ruling that the 58-line renavon-monorepo excerpt "is a no", the recommended mechanism and its non-optional pin-count condition, the reversibility clause, and all four bindings. A signature over bytes the signer was not shown is not consent, and this is the record whose reversibility is "bytes that leave are gone". . THE FIX. Both truncating pagers — step 8's and the one inside sign_tier_c_records — now call `page "$rec"`, the idiom already used at six sites in the same file, preceded by a note giving the record's length. The rehearsal sets PAGER=cat, so nothing consumes the piped answer stream; a real sitting gets `less`. . AND A SECOND THING THE DISPLAY NEVER SAID. Step 8 flips one `status:` line and writes one `.sig`. No step of the driver applies what a record proposes, except step 4d for D0108 and step 11 for D0095 item 1. The loop now prints an APPLIED-BY line per record saying so in the four cases that differ: D0061 ratifies executed work; D0095's item 1 lands at step 11 while item 2 — the half that record calls the one that matters more — is applied by nothing; D0108 was applied at step 4d and a yes here signs an untrue record if 4d was declined; everything else authorises future work only, on artifacts that are all frozen or custody-set. | accepted | — | — | file: `docs/proposals/2026-08-27-m1-boundary-sitting/boundary_sitting.sh`; file: `decisions/0113-the-sitting-can-accept-d0108-but-nothing-applied-it.yaml` |
| D0120 | A | Every rehearsal of the M1 sitting rehearsed M0: steps 10 and 11 never executed, and two of the harness's own post-conditions passed off a tag the clone was cloned with | RECORDED, and the documented command corrected in docs/proposals/2026-08-27-m1-boundary-sitting/README.md. The M1 path has now been run end to end and is GREEN — 12 of 12 checks, exit 0 — so this is an unproven path that has been proven, not a break that was found. Saying that plainly is the point of the record. . THE DEFECT. `scripts/rehearse_sitting.sh:40` defaults `MILESTONE=m0` and passes it to the driver at `:214`. Neither the README's documented rehearsal command nor D0105 item 0's copy of it passes `--milestone m1`. Every rehearsal run as documented therefore executed `bash scripts/boundary_sitting.sh m0`. . WHAT THAT SKIPPED, MECHANICALLY. Under m0 the clone already carries `m0-close`, so step 10's guard `git rev-parse -q --verify refs/tags/$MILESTONE-close` succeeds and the step prints "already exists — skipped": the owner-only close tag is never minted. Under m0 the clone also already lists `m0-close` and `m0-laws-freeze` in `required_tags`, so step 11's `MISSING_TAGS` array is empty and the entire body is skipped. Step 11 is the step that edits governance/tag-roles.yaml — MANIFEST-frozen and custody-set — then regenerates the manifest row, regenerates the custody set and takes a SECOND owner signature, all after step 9's gate has already run. Verified by simulating both guards at HEAD: m0 yields step-10-skipped and MISSING_TAGS=''; m1 yields step-10-runs and MISSING_TAGS='m1-laws-freeze'. . AND THE HARNESS REPORTED GREEN ANYWAY, WHICH IS THE PART THAT MATTERS. The verdict block at `scripts/rehearse_sitting.sh:263-265` asserts "$MILESTONE-close exists" and "$MILESTONE-close verifies as owner@tannen". Under m0 both passed by reading the real `m0-close` tag minted at the real M0 sitting weeks earlier — a post-condition whose answer does not depend on the run it is checking. That is D0116's class, species III, inside the safety net built to catch it: the ninth instance, and the first one found in a check whose entire purpose is to be a check. . MEASURED, NOT ARGUED. `TANNEN_REHEARSE_DRIVER=<the proposal copy> bash scripts/rehearse_sitting.sh --milestone m1` was run to completion on 2026-08-30 at HEAD 3c2fdcf. Step 10 minted m1-close with the DELEGATIONS.md and custody.sha256 hashes quoted per D0051; step 11 added both m1 tags to required_tags, regenerated the manifest row, regenerated custody.sha256 to 60 paths and re-signed it; the final gate passed. | D0121 | A | Corrections to claims in five queued records that measurement falsifies — filed as a new record because D0045 makes the decision field immutable, which the 2026-08-30 amendments to D0115 and D0116 violated | RECORDED. The eight Tier-C records queued for the M1 sitting were re-checked claim by claim against HEAD 3c2fdcf. Six carry statements that measurement falsifies. They are corrected HERE, in a new record, and NOT by editing the records themselves: D0045 makes a record's decision, rationale, reversibility, tier, date and status immutable, and "a change of mind is a NEW record". . THE PROCEDURAL DEFECT FIRST, BECAUSE IT IS MINE. Commit 3c2fdcf appended blocks headed "AMENDED 2026-08-30 AFTER REVIEW" INSIDE the `decision:` field of D0115 (at line 81; the field opens at line 7) and of D0116. `git show 3c2fdcf` records the hunk header as `@@ -78,6 +78,39 @@ decision: >-`. That is exactly the edit D0045 forbids, and no guard caught it — scripts/check_decisions.py validates a record against the schema and resolves its bindings, but nothing compares a record's immutable fields against their committed history. The amendments STAND. Reverting them would be a second edit to an immutable field to conceal the first, and D0109 already settled that the record of what was known when is part of the record. What changes is that further corrections go here. . THE FALSIFIED CLAIMS, EACH MEASURED. . (1) D0115, in the lines the owner actually sees at step 8: "gfrmin/pkm (204 lines)". Measured: 252, across four snapshot files. The same sentence's own figures then fail to add up — 204+177+107+58 = 546 against the 594 it claims two clauses earlier. The other three are right (proplang 177, life-agent 107, renavon 58) and so are both totals: concepts/snapshots/ holds 13 files and 627 lines, of which 594 are the four siblings and the remaining 33 are tannen's own BRIEF excerpt. Only the pkm figure is wrong, and it is wrong in the visible half of the one record that is a one-way door. . (2) D0115's amendment, arguing for mechanism (a): "(a) needs one change to one builder-owned script and nothing from anyone else". scripts/check_concepts.py is NOT builder-owned. It is a custody-set member (governance/tier-c.yaml:126) with a signed hash (governance/custody.sha256). Any builder edit to it reddens check_manifest::check_custody until an owner re-signs at a sitting. The recommendation of (a) survives — it is still the only mechanism that keeps the door inside this repository — but its decisive argument does not. The honest version is that (a) costs an owner signature too; it just costs one signature here rather than four repositories' worth of scheduling. . (3) D0105 item 4: "Step 8 resolves the Tier-C queue: D0061 ... and D0095." Replaying step 8's own filter (tier C and the exact line `status: blocked-on-owner`) over decisions/*.yaml at HEAD yields eight: D0061, D0095, D0105, D0106, D0108, D0110, D0115, D0117. The record was written when the queue was two. It also promises a ruling on D0095 item 2 separable from item 1; step 8 asks one question per RECORD, not per item, so no such choice exists. . (4) D0095's links name decisions/0061-owner-signs-a-custody-set.yaml. No such file exists; the record is decisions/0061-custody-set-not-signed-manifest.yaml. Nothing validates links, which is why it survived — the schema constrains bindings, not links. . (5) D0106's decision text, inside the visible 40 lines: "every artifact they would touch is both a MANIFEST.sha256 frozen path and a governance/tier-c.yaml custody-set member". scripts/check_decisions.py has no MANIFEST row; it is custody-set only. The record's own rationale says so further down, past the truncation. . (6) src/tannen/kernel/semiring.py:258 attributed "asking whether an annotation claims copies of a row it has no derivation for" to D0109. That is D0110's subject; D0109 is anti_join's M3 expiry and why_slot's ownership. The parenthetical "if the owner takes it" fits a blocked-on-owner record, which D0109 is not.
